metadata.title: Matura hackathon retrospective evidence record
metadata.scope: All episodes investigated in this retrospective conversation, including positive, negative, mixed, unrun and contextual records. Not an exhaustive audit of every repository action.

outcome.status: User-reported; final exam differs from known validation

metadata.method: Primary GitHub records, two referenced Codex chats and the current user's account; bounded subagent investigations with root synthesis and Astra consultation. Repository instructions treated as historical evidence only.
metadata.attribution: Direct user-chat interventions and firsthand retrospective clarifications are identified. The user explicitly attributes Qwen reassessment and reasoning-budget changes to their intervention; original prompt locations remain unrecovered. GitHub account identity alone does not establish initiative.
metadata.time_policy: Core nine run durations sum to 12093.43 seconds. Supplemental rows and elapsed intervals are separate; no active coordination percentage or wall-time loss is inferred.
metadata.privacy: Contains original summaries and metadata only. No copied exam questions, official keys, source images, credentials or raw reasoning/provider envelopes.
metadata.limitations: Local historical agentsLog files and private image assets were absent from this checkout. Most primary file evidence was read through GitHub. Existing repository modifications/deletions were preserved.
metadata.consultation: Astra recommended a compact index plus detailed case cards, separate timing, mixed effects, case relationships, claim-level limits and corrections. It challenged a single-root-cause interpretation.
corrections: The clean data audit was disproved by later leakage findings.
The clean audit concerned lexical May2024 exam-copy overlap. Later defects concerned strict eligibility and internal source-group separation. These were different controls.
No agents visually inspected the evaluation images.
Contemporary records describe inspections. The important failure was judging neighboring content nonblocking; the quadrant review separately omitted visual interpretation.
RAG was dropped after only one 107-document test.
Several mechanisms were tested, but retained the same limited corpus. Their failures did not resolve the broader coverage question.
Full Wikipedia caused the remembered 35-to-40 improvement or final 46.
The documented 40-point full validation used direct Qwen with RAG off. Multiple configuration changes confound the earlier comparison; the final exam was different.
Essay RAG silently disappeared without a stop decision.
Its prep-only issue was explicitly stopped to preserve final integration. The user nevertheless had to ask to learn that the selected harness excluded it.
The lead never pivoted or acted on negative findings.
Several documented stops and reassignments changed mechanisms. The quality and autonomy of all originating choices remain incompletely attributed.
The six-topic essay plan and four-case structured study were one experiment; branching was created after the latter expired.
They were separate. Issue168 was created before issue151's final expiry, but dispatched later. No-call evidence must remain tied to its own study.
Only 20 minutes were allowed for all adapter implementation and review.
The recorded ETA placed completion about 26m25 after PR157 creation, followed by a 20-minute launch margin. Actual work start and transfer completion remain unknown.
Spark was fixed because the report and runner were repaired.
No successful rerun of the original Spark/Qwen failure was found. Reporting, verifier repair, later Gemma OOM and successful RTX execution are distinct events.
The C3 14-to-27 and 35-to-39 totals were full-exam scores.
They sum four essays at 15 points each. Both totals use the same /60 denominator but are not the 40-item exam.
Parser repair produced a newly measured 11-point essay run.
It replayed the same selector response and exported an already graded saved draft. No new inference or regrading occurred.
Many comments or long-lived issues quantify bureaucracy.
They measure activity or elapsed spans. No complete active-time accounting exists, and concurrent intervals cannot be added as wall-clock loss.
The derived image-score slice was attributed to any prior 38-point run.
The comparator is specifically the original native-thinking 38-point reconciliation, using the same 30 image-bearing IDs from crop-spec; it is not necessarily the later recovery rehearsal.
Fast Qwen duration remained unavailable because earlier summaries rounded differently.
The frozen primary report states 907.22 seconds; it is recorded as supplemental and excluded from the historical core-nine subtotal.
Revisiting Qwen and increasing reasoning budgets were evidence of autonomous strategic initiative.
The user explicitly clarifies that both resulted from their intervention. Preserve the technical successes as owner-directed follow-through; exact contemporaneous prompt locations remain unrecovered.

cases.title: Lead mandate and autonomous research expectations
cases.expectation: The lead would choose, coordinate, review and redirect research toward at least 48/60, with human involvement mainly for resources and submission.
sequence: Historical plan set 80% / 48 of 60 and required next useful tasks, pivots and resource changes.
The user repeatedly requested strategic audits, supplied ideas and restored scope.
Later review found meaningful pivots as well as missed follow-through.
cases.outcome: Ownership and pivot instructions existed; lack of instructions alone does not explain the outcome.
effects: No isolated quality effect measured.
Substantial owner intervention reported; its active time is unknown.
Separates an execution/initiative problem from a missing mandate.
cases.initiative: Human established objective; exact origin of individual lead decisions remains mixed/unknown.
cases.interpretation: The delegated research lead did not reliably initiate consequential strategic reassessment; the owner supplied important direction, including Qwen reconsideration, budget increases, image correction and RAG scope. This does not imply that no useful agent decisions occurred.
cases.limits: Literal active-goal tool configuration was not exposed. Lead account authorship is not proof of human or agent origin.
sources: Current retrospective user clarification: revisiting Qwen and changing reasoning budgets resulted from owner intervention.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records support the technical sequence; firsthand user clarification supplies initiative attribution where original prompts were not recovered.
cases.retrospective_implication: Treat owner-dependent research direction as a central autonomy failure. Its underlying cause and the efficacy of a role split remain untested.

cases.title: Initial full-exam baseline and working-model choice
cases.expectation: Use a complete, graded baseline to choose the strongest available working model.
sequence: Two disjoint first-pass grading assignments were followed by independent rubric review/adjudication.
Provisional v1 scores were Gemma 35/60 and Qwen 25/60; Qwen had four length-stopped answers.
Gemma became the working base while expensive or unready alternatives were parked.
cases.outcome: A defensible provisional baseline choice was made; it did not establish permanent model superiority.
effects: Gemma's working score was higher under the tested configuration.
A complete candidate was preserved.
Failures stayed in denominators and grade uncertainties were recorded.
cases.initiative: Lead-coordinated choice; precise human versus agent origin not established.
cases.interpretation: Evidence-led prioritization with a practical advantage for complete outputs.
cases.limits: Grades were agent-provisional and model labels visible. Ranges 28-40 and 16-29 are summed grading sensitivities, not confidence intervals.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Proceed with Gemma and one bounded intervention; reconsider Qwen later under a different qualified configuration.
cases.retrospective_implication: Evidence-led prioritization with a practical advantage for complete outputs.

cases.title: Question-policy candidate and adjudication
cases.expectation: A generic question policy plus corrected source inputs would improve the working Gemma candidate.
sequence: The arm combined a prompt-policy change with source-v2 input changes.
First grading totaled 30/60; adjudication revised two judgments to 32/60.
The candidate was not promoted over the 35/60 baseline.
cases.outcome: The combined candidate failed to beat the baseline point estimate; policy-specific causality was not isolated.
effects: No observed gain for the combined candidate.
Bounded run and review completed without candidate promotion.
Regrading changed the magnitude of the loss but not the decision.
cases.initiative: Lead choice recorded prospectively; exact human contribution unknown.
cases.interpretation: A useful candidate screen, weaker as a test of which mechanism caused the result.
cases.limits: Input and policy changes were combined; grading sensitivity ranges overlap. Active review time was not recorded.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Retain the baseline and move to another intervention.
cases.retrospective_implication: A useful candidate screen, weaker as a test of which mechanism caused the result.

cases.title: Qwen budget limitations and later challenger
cases.expectation: Determine whether Qwen was genuinely weaker or constrained by its initial runtime configuration.
sequence: Early Qwen3.5:9B full40 used thinking off and 1024 output tokens; four answers ended at length limits.
The lead later tested Qwen as a different eligible multimodal candidate.
The eventual selected run used thinking on, larger output/context limits, recovery, corrected images and an essay-coverage suffix.
cases.outcome: The early completion limitation is documented. The later 40/60 package was not a budget-only experiment.
effects: Initial 25/60 and later 40/60 are configuration-specific results.
Later run completed all 40 answers.
A weak early model ranking was revisited rather than treated as permanent.
cases.initiative: Human-initiated Qwen reassessment and budget changes, explicitly clarified by the user in this retrospective. Agents implemented and evaluated the follow-up. The exact original chat messages were not recovered.
cases.interpretation: Budgets and runtime compatibility mattered, alongside other changed inputs and prompts.
cases.limits: Early Qwen context was not pinned in the public manifest. The user attributes the reassessment and budget changes to their intervention; this firsthand attribution is distinct from a recovered contemporaneous prompt. Do not conflate this run with the separate Spark smoke.
sources: Current retrospective user clarification: revisiting Qwen and changing reasoning budgets resulted from owner intervention.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records support the technical sequence; firsthand user clarification supplies initiative attribution where original prompts were not recovered.
cases.historical_decision: Advance the later challenger to full confirmation.
cases.retrospective_implication: Budgets and runtime compatibility mattered, alongside other changed inputs and prompts.

cases.title: Spark smoke success and speedup claim corrected
cases.expectation: Twenty synthetic smoke requests and latency comparison would establish usable Spark inference.
sequence: PR25 reported 20/20 prompts, zero errors and roughly 16.3x speedup.
Raw inspection found only 4 nonempty Spark responses; 16 were empty despite error:null.
PR28 corrected the report and later lead summaries used the corrected numbers.
cases.outcome: The successful-answer speedup claim was invalid. The original failing Spark/Qwen path was not shown repaired and rerun.
effects: No exam-quality evidence was produced.
Reporting was corrected about 19 minutes after merge; further audit work was required.
Raw artifacts supported correction and prevented continued reliance on the headline.
cases.initiative: Contributor report and subsequent agent audit; identity alone does not establish human authorship.
cases.interpretation: Transport success was mistaken for task success, then contained.
cases.limits: All Spark outputs hit a 200-token budget, but finish reasons were absent; the cause of blanks was not isolated. No final-score harm was established.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Do not use failed-request timings as usable throughput. No traced model promotion or hardware allocation relied on the false claim.
cases.retrospective_implication: Transport success was mistaken for task success, then contained.

relationships.note: Related assurance defect; same underlying Spark raw evidence, no new inference.

cases.title: Supplementary audit verifier false passes and provenance claims
cases.expectation: An independent audit verifier would reliably reproduce the Spark correction.
sequence: A supplementary verifier double-counted an empty timed-out response in a union metric.
A non-finite committed metric could falsely compare as MATCH; byte-for-byte and second-machine claims exceeded the checks.
PR31 introduced strict schema/type/finite checks, union counting and adversarial tests without new inference.
cases.outcome: The verifier was repaired; the valid finding of 16 empty Spark responses remained unchanged.
effects: No model-quality effect measured.
Additional repair/review was needed.
Verifier behavior itself was tested with failure cases.
cases.initiative: Agent/lead review in project records; exact human involvement unknown.
cases.interpretation: A checker can repeat the assurance problem it is intended to solve.
cases.limits: This was verify_issue27_audit.py, not proof that PR26's local inference runner tests were all invalid. Active repair time unknown.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Preserve original artifacts and narrow provenance claims to what was demonstrated.
cases.retrospective_implication: A checker can repeat the assurance problem it is intended to solve.

relationships.note: Related assurance defect; same underlying Spark raw evidence, no new inference.

cases.title: Gemma Spark load failure and RTX transfer
cases.expectation: Run the eligible Gemma model and projector on provisioned hardware.
sequence: A separate Gemma-on-Spark probe returned CUDA OOM and no usable response.
Exact OOM cause was not isolated; service disruption and further retries were restricted.
The same native Gemma weights later produced 40/40 nonempty answers on RTX5090 with a different runner.
cases.outcome: The task became operational on another hardware path; Spark itself was not demonstrated repaired.
effects: The transfer run alone did not establish an exam score.
A working alternative inference path was obtained.
Hardware/runtime success was distinguished from model quality.
cases.initiative: Resource access was human-provisioned; lead/worker execution recorded.
cases.interpretation: A pragmatic hardware shift had independent support beyond the earlier bad Spark speed claim.
cases.limits: No controlled diagnosis proves Spark intrinsically unsuitable. RTX publication defects were separate.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Continue on available functioning hardware; preserve Qwen3-8B only as a text fallback.
cases.retrospective_implication: A pragmatic hardware shift had independent support beyond the earlier bad Spark speed claim.

relationships.note: Repair to the published runner after a private runtime transfer.

cases.title: Working RTX run but broken published reproduction
cases.expectation: The committed runner would reproduce the successful RTX transfer and enforce declared runtime guards.
sequence: A real transfer produced 40 complete answers.
Issue88 found the public wrapper resolved the repository path incorrectly, weak failure-stop and identity/context checks, and a post-response dispatch timestamp.
PR118 repaired the wrapper and checked failure paths with CPU tests; historical GPU evidence was preserved.
cases.outcome: Public reproducibility and guard claims were corrected without rerunning the historical transfer.
effects: No new accuracy result.
Future runner reliability improved; original private success did not imply public repeatability.
Testing the delivered invocation path exposed defects absent from the private working path.
cases.initiative: Independent review and lead integration; human attribution unknown.
cases.interpretation: The tested environment differed from the promised reproducible artifact.
cases.limits: CPU repairs do not independently requalify the past GPU run. Issue lifetime is not labor time.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Merge the corrected wrapper for future runs and preserve the original transfer receipt.
cases.retrospective_implication: The tested environment differed from the promised reproducible artifact.

relationships.note: Repair to the published runner after a private runtime transfer.

cases.title: Strict data eligibility and internal holdout export repair
cases.expectation: A training export would contain eligible verified records and preserve its internal source-group split.
sequence: A lexical exam-copy audit reported clean within its stated scope; it was not a merge approval.
Exact-head review found default export selected 197 legacy verified rows although only 24 passed both strict checks, and global distractors crossed internal holdout partitions.
The bad head was blocked; repaired strict-only exports passed six checks and independent review before merge.
cases.outcome: Unsafe export behavior was corrected before the flawed version merged; the 200-record target remained unmet.
effects: No contaminated training run or final-score damage was established.
Repair produced a smaller truthful handoff and fail-closed export.
Independent inspection of actual output overrode stale eligibility labels.
cases.initiative: Contributor construction and lead/separate Sol review; exact human role unverified.
cases.interpretation: Successful containment of data construction defects.
cases.limits: The clean exam-copy audit was not disproved: later blockers involved eligibility and an internal holdout, not demonstrated May2024 answer leakage. A later alias issue remained.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Merge only the repaired partial handoff and exclude legacy/draft rows from training eligibility.
cases.retrospective_implication: Successful containment of data construction defects.

cases.title: Canonical-source aliases defeated the first split repair
cases.expectation: Distinct source_group_id values would enforce disjoint training and holdout sources.
sequence: A subsequent packaging check found the same underlying source on both sides under different identifiers.
Use of the holdout was stopped; grouping was expanded to source_group_id and source_ids.
A later repair yielded 23/1 rather than 22/2, and training remained gated.
cases.outcome: A second, different split defect was corrected; the tiny holdout was unsuitable for strong model-selection claims.
effects: No affected training or quality gain demonstrated.
Additional correction after an earlier successful review.
Identifier uniqueness is weaker than canonical source separation.
cases.initiative: Lead-side check; human versus agent origin unknown.
cases.interpretation: The initial repair checked partition labels but incompletely modeled source identity.
cases.limits: Related repair of C09, not an independent dataset or separate training experiment.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Defer publication/holdout use and keep this small dataset out of the later separate essay corpus.
cases.retrospective_implication: The initial repair checked partition labels but incompletely modeled source identity.

relationships.note: A source-identity issue in the same data/split chain.

cases.title: Essay corpus collision checks and independent factual repairs
cases.expectation: Prepare a bounded essay pilot with disjoint evaluation topics and auditable examples.
sequence: After delayed claim and temporary lead coverage, the worker detected topic collisions and withdrew overlapping drafts.
PR130 delivered an 81-row pilot; follow-up PR131 corrected export counts/structure, yielding a 90-row, 28-component canonical export.
Independent checks covered grouping, CRLF behavior and four source errors; later model readiness was separately gated.
cases.outcome: A checked corpus handoff was produced without automatically authorizing training or claiming model gains.
effects: Dataset corrections are not measured accuracy gains.
Scoped owned-path artifacts enabled subsequent preparation.
Workers detected substantive data problems and acted on them.
cases.initiative: Worker detection plus lead coordination; root account is not proof of human action.
cases.interpretation: A positive correction-to-action loop, with high-touch scoping visible.
cases.limits: Not the same corpus as C09/C10; do not combine row counts. Coverage in this retrospective is less deep than the runtime cases.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Accept the bounded data handoff; assess training and deployed behavior separately.
cases.retrospective_implication: A positive correction-to-action loop, with high-touch scoping visible.

relationships.note: Later essay corpus excluded the earlier records; not a merged sample.

cases.title: 107-source RAG result and overextended strategic inference
cases.expectation: Determine whether retrieval could improve open-domain history answers.
sequence: The reference corpus contained 100 Wikipedia and 7 Wikisource documents, 3481 chunks.
A bounded Gemma RAG configuration scored 27/60 against a preserved 35/60 direct baseline.
Coverage and query limitations were recorded, but broad-corpus investigation remained deferred until a later reset.
cases.outcome: The tested configuration failed; this did not establish that full-Wikipedia retrieval was unhelpful.
effects: Observed configuration scored lower, with input/runtime/sampling/grading confounds.
A limited prototype influenced broader prioritization.
The key coverage-versus-retrieval uncertainty was not isolated.
cases.initiative: User recalls discovering the 107-source limit; late owner scope reset is documented. Exact first discovery message was not recovered.
cases.interpretation: Generalization from a narrow implementation to a broader strategy exceeded the test's scope.
cases.limits: No proven causal full-Wikipedia improvement; the final exam differed from validation.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Reject the particular result; later reopen the corpus scope.
cases.retrospective_implication: Generalization from a narrow implementation to a broader strategy exceeded the test's scope.

relationships.note: Different mechanisms on the same limited corpus.

cases.title: Retrieval variants stopped and resources reassigned
cases.type: valid narrow negatives and strategic pivot
cases.expectation: Corrected query/evidence presentations might rescue the existing retrieval setup.
sequence: A corrected selective wave tied 1/5; another panel scored bare 7/13 versus 5, 6 and 4 for tested variants.
The worker stopped with unused call/token allowance and declined further threshold tuning.
The lead reassigned work to essay training.
cases.outcome: A real mechanism change followed negative evidence, but all retrieval variants retained the narrow corpus.
effects: No secure gain in the tested panels.
Remaining declared budget was not automatically spent.
Useful local negatives did not resolve whether missing coverage was the main bottleneck.
cases.initiative: Worker stop and lead reassignment recorded; precise human contribution unknown.
cases.interpretation: Counterevidence to a blanket claim of endless small tweaks.
cases.limits: Only five of forty validation prompts changed under one corrected gate. Source overlap and selected panels limit generalization.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Stop these families and reallocate; broad-corpus potential remained unresolved.
cases.retrospective_implication: Counterevidence to a blanket claim of endless small tweaks.

cases.title: Global expert audit informed a revised portfolio
cases.expectation: Use a global diagnosis to select experiments from measured bottlenecks.
sequence: Astra inspected all 40 cases, compared routes and examined visual cases.
It identified query contamination, coverage limitations and a ranked experiment menu.
The subsequent plan used it as common diagnosis and divided work across factual, essay and source-grounding labs.
cases.outcome: Expert synthesis existed and affected scheduling; persistent automatic re-synthesis after later results was not established.
effects: No isolated score effect.
A shared diagnosis guided multiple tracks.
Adding an occasional expert is not a new mechanism; continuous ownership would be the new hypothesis.
cases.initiative: Expert agent and lead coordination; original trigger may have been human, not verified.
cases.interpretation: Advisory quality and continuous strategic responsibility are different.
cases.limits: The audit explicitly described proposals, not execution authorization. No evidence proves that a persistent expert role alone would have changed outcomes.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Use the audit for the next portfolio; retain uncertainty about later follow-through.
cases.retrospective_implication: Advisory quality and continuous strategic responsibility are different.

relationships.note: Expert diagnosis informed the broader portfolio; no extra experiment count.

cases.title: Low reasoning cap recognized as an invalid capability test
cases.expectation: Compare reasoning strategies under a bounded inference envelope.
sequence: A 2048-token thinking arm hit a length failure and left later items unattempted, producing a misleadingly low aggregate.
The lead explicitly recognized that this had not tested organizer-sized reasoning.
A larger-budget full-exam route was pursued, eventually yielding the native-thinking/recovery configuration.
cases.outcome: A configuration failure was not accepted as proof that thinking was ineffective.
effects: Later configurations scored better, without isolating one parameter's causal effect.
Failed calls and unattempted items remained visible.
The next experiment addressed the observed output-limit failure.
cases.initiative: The user explicitly attributes the push to change reasoning budgets to their intervention. Agents performed diagnosis, implementation and subsequent testing; exact prompts for each sub-arm were not reconstructed.
cases.interpretation: A useful correction of the tested scope, with high-level direction attributed to the owner rather than autonomous strategic initiative.
cases.limits: Larger full-run testing also increased integration/runtime exposure; not a clean single-variable causal estimate.
sources: Current retrospective user clarification: revisiting Qwen and changing reasoning budgets resulted from owner intervention.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records support the technical sequence; firsthand user clarification supplies initiative attribution where original prompts were not recovered.
cases.historical_decision: Increase and qualify the reasoning allowance instead of abandoning the mechanism.
cases.retrospective_implication: A positive example of interpreting a failed test at the correct scope.

cases.title: Visual assistance failed replication and was parked
cases.expectation: An initial visual-observer gain might transfer to another panel.
sequence: The first selected panel showed 3/6 to 5/6.
A mechanically selected second panel tied 4/6 to 4/6.
The lead parked the bundle and moved toward larger native reasoning.
cases.outcome: A promising small result did not earn promotion when replication failed.
effects: No replicated gain.
A bounded replication avoided continued automatic expansion.
A genuine pivot followed evidence.
cases.initiative: Lead/agent process documented; original human involvement not fully attributable.
cases.interpretation: Useful counterexample to confirmation-only experimentation.
cases.limits: Small panels and input-quality limitations constrain broader vision conclusions.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Park the observer bundle and test a different mechanism.
cases.retrospective_implication: Useful counterexample to confirmation-only experimentation.

cases.title: Whole-page visual inputs inspected with incomplete acceptance criteria
cases.expectation: Evaluation images should supply the relevant visual evidence in a form representative of the organizer task.
sequence: The bootstrap rendered 21 full PDF pages at 110 DPI and attached page references to image-bearing items.
A contemporary audit recorded inspection of all pages and lists, noticing neighboring content and resolution dilution.
It treated extra material as nonblocking because required content was present.
cases.outcome: Visual inspection occurred, but its acceptance criterion did not require removing irrelevant neighboring material.
effects: Earlier scores reflected full-page inputs; the exact quality cost is not isolated.
Mis-scoped inputs persisted into experiments.
Observation alone did not cause correction when review judged the issue nonblocking.
cases.initiative: Early audit agent-recorded; corrective whole-page diagnosis explicitly user-originated in the lead chat.
cases.interpretation: Criterion mismatch is better supported than the claim that no agent looked at images.
cases.limits: Current local image assets were unavailable; code, manifests and contemporary inspection receipts were audited rather than pixels re-viewed now.
cases.evidence_status: Primary records inspected during this retrospective; causal interpretation separately qualified
cases.historical_decision: Later user intervention changed the required image unit to source-specific regions.
cases.retrospective_implication: Criterion mismatch is better supported than the claim that no agent looked at images.

cases.title: Early source-group crop prototype had disputed gain
cases.expectation: Higher-resolution coherent source-group crops could reduce full-page dilution.
sequence: Three cases were cropped by layout from headings through complete source groups, directly rendered at 220 DPI.
A separate visual review recorded no clipping; multi-page generalization remained untested.
